choices: Months are calendar months of the dates in the file; a month's days are the file rows falling in it; the monthly factor return compounds those rows in file order.

The 126-day variance window is the 126 rows of the same file immediately preceding the month's first row, regardless of which months those rows fall in; v_m is undefined when fewer than 126 rows precede, and the month is then excluded from every range.
A realised variance of exactly zero raises rather than producing an infinite weight.

Completeness: every month before the file's last month is complete; the last month is complete only if the file's last date equals the last Monday-to-Friday calendar day of that month (a holiday falling on that day makes the month incomplete, as the rule is written).

In-sample = months with v_m defined AND complete, from the first such month to 2015-12 inclusive; OOS = months with v_m defined AND complete from 2016-01 to the last complete month. If the file ends before 2016 the OOS is empty and the verdict INSUFFICIENT.
A gap (missing calendar month) inside the in-sample or OOS range raises; months are not silently skipped.

Criterion (a) regresses managed on raw (R* = a + b R + e) with an intercept; the Newey-West sandwich uses Bartlett weights 1 - l/(L+1), L = 3, and no small-sample or degrees-of-freedom correction; t = a / se(a); the test is a > 0 and t >= 2.0.
Sharpe = sqrt(12) x mean / sd with ddof = 1, applied to monthly returns; the ratio reported is Sharpe(R*) / Sharpe(R), null if Sharpe(R) is exactly zero.

Criterion (b)'s 'at least 1.2 x the raw Sharpe' is applied as a gain test, per the coordinator's clarification of 29 October 2026 treated as part of the specification: (Sharpe(R*) - Sharpe(R)) >= 0.2 x |Sharpe(R)| and p_boot <= 0.05. For a positive raw Sharpe this is identical to the 1.2 x rule; for a raw Sharpe at or below zero, where a ratio is meaningless, it requires an improvement of 0.2 x |raw|.

Bootstrap: one rng = default_rng(20261029) per test; each of the 10,000 draws makes one call rng.integers(0, n, size=ceil(n/12)) (sequential calls, not one vectorised call); blocks are start, start+1, ..., start+11 modulo n, concatenated in draw order and truncated to n; the difference is Sharpe(R*[idx]) - Sharpe(R[idx]) with the same formula as the headline Sharpe; a draw with difference <= 0 (or NaN, which fails the comparison) is counted as not positive. The MTUM test re-seeds a fresh rng.
Criteria a and b are reported as computed even when the verdict is INSUFFICIENT; the 96-month floor sets the verdict only. With fewer than 3 months the statistics are null and the criteria false.

Maximum drawdown: wealth path W_0 = 1, W_t = W_(t-1)(1 + R_t); drawdown_t = W_t / max(W_0..W_t) - 1; reported value is the minimum (a non-positive fraction, 0 if wealth never falls below its running peak).
Weight distribution over OOS months: numpy min, median (mean of the two middle values when n is even) and max; share above 2 is the fraction of months with w_m strictly greater than 2.
Worst months: OOS months sorted ascending by raw R_m (ties by calendar order), the first five, each with the managed return of the same month.

MTUM version: daily returns r_t = P_t / P_(t-1) - 1 from consecutive rows of bench.csv where both closes are present (NaN otherwise); the spread day series is the set of rows where both r_MTUM and r_SPY are defined; months, monthly products and the 126-day window are taken over that day series only, so the two legs are always compounded over identical days. S_m = prod(1 + r_MTUM) - prod(1 + r_SPY), not prod(1 + d) - 1.
MTUM completeness is judged against the last date of bench.csv (its last SPY trading day), not against mom_daily.csv.
MTUM test range: every month with v_m defined and complete, with no in-sample/OOS split; the same 96-month floor, criteria and verdict labels apply.

Cost estimate: 0.0020 x sum over m = 2..n of |w_m - w_(m-1)|, divided by n/12 years (the first month's establishment of the position is not charged); ann_return_managed is the arithmetic 12 x mean of the managed monthly spread, in the same units as the cost.
Inputs are validated: dates must be strictly increasing, Mom must not be blank, closes must be positive; any violation raises rather than being repaired.
